solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Restrain daring writer from Spooner's lips

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so the two words are said with their starts exchanged

parts.note: daring means bold; its first sound is swapped with that of the next word
a hack is a jobbing writer; its first sound is swapped with that of the previous word

explanation.surface: A plea to keep a bold author from speaking out of turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reverend Spooner was an Oxford don said to swap the opening sounds of neighbouring words.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in check or stop it advancing is to restrain it.

clue.text: Game Charlie punches artificial American

indicators.note: a fist punches into something, so one piece is driven inside another

parts.note: hokey is American slang for contrived or fake
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sports report about a man called Charlie throwing a punch at a phoney American.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside HOKEY to make HOCKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockey is a team sport played with sticks and a ball or puck, an example of a game.

clue.text: Son must give the slip to thin creditor

indicators.note: to give someone the slip is to escape from them, so this letter leaves the word

parts.note: slender means thin
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son has to escape a lean moneylender who is chasing a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: SLENDER loses its S to leave LENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who advances money and is owed it back is a creditor.

clue.text: Acting group in support of vulgar show on TV

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporter sits below, so the acting group comes under the other word

parts.note: broad humour is coarse or vulgar
the cast is the group of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Actors propping up a crude television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'in support of' puts CAST beneath BROAD, holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit a programme over the airwaves for viewers is to air or screen it.

clue.text: Celtic lovely when playing as a team

indicators.note: players move around the pitch, so these letters move into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Celtic, the Glasgow football club, look lovely when they play together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something jointly, with everyone acting together as one unit, is doing it collectively.

clue.text: Bad officer cut down in midst of attack

indicators.note: being in the midst of something means sitting inside it

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

indicators.note: something cut down is shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A wartime scene of an officer killed during an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' looks like killed in battle; here it just trims the last letter off the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off and smells sour is said to have gone bad.

clue.text: Vote to eject Bob at summit! Dole out!

indicators.note: ejecting something throws it out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a ballot is a vote

indicators.note: the summit is the top, so only the head letter of that name is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of Bob

explanation.surface: Campaign slogans: vote out Bob at the summit and hand out the spoils.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the B of BALLOT is at the top; removing it leaves ALLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion shares among people, which is to dole them out.

clue.text: Mostly potty American leader and tyrant

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a commode is a chair containing a chamber pot
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A jibe at a crazy American president who behaves like a despot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like an adjective meaning crazy; it is the noun, a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodus was a Roman emperor of the second century notorious for cruelty and megalomania.

clue.text: Untidy she-devil needs sorting out

indicators.note: sorting out puts things in a different order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A messy woman with a fiery temper needs taking in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untidy' is a verb here, to make untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel hair or clothes is to disarrange them, making them messy.

clue.text: Pet loves being surrounded by light

indicators.note: one thing surrounded by another ends up inside it

parts.note: a candle gives light
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A pet animal is cherished by candlelight, or loves the glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal but is a verb, to fondle; love is nought in tennis scores, written as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, the same as to pet.

clue.text: They could be walkers on cold hills

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing placed on another follows it, so the walkers come after

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
legs are limbs, and legs walk

explanation.surface: Hikers out on chilly fells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walkers on cold hills' reads as ramblers; the definition is just 'hills', and LIMBS goes on after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an ascent or upward slope, so steep inclines and hills are climbs.

clue.text: Gone off with our nurse? One might do that!

definitions.text: Gone off with our nurse? One might do that!

indicators.note: something gone off has gone bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: part of the letters to rearrange
the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Hospital gossip: has the surgeon run off with our nurse?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of a hospital doctor eloping with a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain surgeon is a senior hospital doctor, the kind famous in fiction for affairs with nursing staff.

clue.text: Conclusion about yours truly is correct

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the end is the conclusion
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A smug claim that one's final verdict is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' is a verb here, not an adjective agreeing with the conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to remove its errors by revising it, so to put it right.

clue.text: Return baton given to English conductor

parts.note: to return a candidate is to elect them
a baton is a rod
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An orchestra hands its baton back to an English maestro.
explanation.walkthrough: The conductor is electrical, not musical; 'Return' means elect, as an MP is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal through which current enters or leaves, an electrical conductor.

clue.text: Sailors with cheek to catch European dressing

indicators.note: catching something takes it in, so a letter is held within

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, so two of them
sauce is impudence, cheek
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Insolent seamen try to nab someone from the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Tar is old slang for a sailor; two of them are needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare sauce is a mayonnaise-based condiment served with fish, a type of dressing.

clue.text: Slim, wise man losing pound for looker abroad?

indicators.note: losing something means it goes, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: slight means slim
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
a seer is a wise prophet

explanation.surface: A lean sage short of cash goes looking for a pretty foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIGHT without L gives SIGHT, then SEER. 'Looker' suggests a beauty; here it is one who looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist goes about viewing famous places, often in foreign countries, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Private last to run aboard navy helicopter

indicators.note: going aboard a craft means getting inside it

parts.note: the Sea King was a naval helicopter used by the Royal Navy

indicators.note: the last to is the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of run

explanation.surface: A private soldier, the last to scramble on board a naval helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes after the S of SEAKING. 'Private' looks like a soldier but is an adjective, as in a sneaking suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneaking feeling is one kept secret or not openly admitted, hence private.

clue.text: Desk, after a grunt, is easily moved

parts.note: taken as written
grunt is US slang for an infantry soldier, a GI
a desk is a kind of table

explanation.surface: An office desk, after someone grunts, proves light to shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grunt' looks like a noise; it is US army slang for an ordinary foot soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitable means capable of being stirred up or disturbed, so readily shaken or moved.

clue.text: Engineer giving teens a minus mark

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so these letters are built into something new

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An engineering teacher hands teenagers a poor grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a person but is a verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol written before a number to show it is below zero is the minus symbol.

clue.text: State prison lawyer in US tours close to Alabama

indicators.note: touring goes around a place, so the outer letters circle the inner one

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
a DA is a district attorney in America

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of Alabama

explanation.surface: An American attorney visits a jail near the state line of Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' tempts toward one of the US states; it means a sovereign nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A state can mean an independent country, and Canada is a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Respect Queen demanding that soprano leaves

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: severe means harsh, demanding
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A queen insists that the singer walk out and treat her with respect.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVERE loses its S, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to hold them in deep esteem or awe, which is to respect them.

clue.text: A curt liar gets high using joints

indicators.note: someone who gets high is out of their head, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rude fibber gets stoned on cannabis cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joints' suggest cannabis; here they are the body's joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Articular is the anatomical adjective for things relating to or involving the body's joints.

clue.text: Conservative slant with no endorsements

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lean is a slant or tilt

explanation.surface: A Tory bias that no backers will support.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, endorsements are penalty points on a driving licence; a licence without them is spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean driving licence has no penalty points recorded against the holder.

clue.text: Line of traffic

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one's line of work or business
second meaning: to deal or buy and sell

explanation.walkthrough: 'Line of traffic' suggests a queue of cars; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade means an occupation or business, and as a verb it means to deal commercially.

clue.text: Bit of restlessness during sleeping is natural

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: someone sleeping is in bed

indicators.note: a bit is just a small part, here the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of restlessness

explanation.surface: A little tossing and turning in your sleep is perfectly normal.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside IN BED.
explanation.definitionFit: An inbred quality is innate, present from birth rather than learned, hence natural.

clue.text: Head of brewery, always with time for a drink

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of brewery
ever means always
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The brewery boss always makes time for a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any liquid for drinking other than water, a drink.

clue.text: Renowned writer, but inexperienced on radio

indicators.note: radio is heard and not seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: green means inexperienced, and the surname sounds the same

explanation.surface: A famous author who is a novice at broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an acclaimed English novelist, author of Brighton Rock and The Third Man.

clue.text: Rise at home and pack in bags last of gear

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to pack in is to stop, cease

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of gear

explanation.surface: Getting up at home and stuffing kit into luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like luggage but is a verb: CEASE bags R. 'Pack in' means stop, not fill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in prices or numbers is a growth, an increase.
